info.name: Simple Bank API
info.description: Start the backend first (./mvnw spring-boot:run), and set the adminEmail and adminPassword collection variables (Current value) to the ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD the backend was started with. Then run the whole collection with the Runner, folders in order. Requests send the customer's token by default (collection-level Bearer auth); admin-only requests use the admin's token, and register/login send none. 'Log in (admin)' gets the staff token. 'Happy path' registers a customer, logs in, and exercises every feature. 'Business rules and errors' checks every rule's status code. 'Security (401 and 403)' checks logins, forged tokens, and that customers can't reach each other's data or staff endpoints. 'Cleanup' deletes everything that was created. Each run uses a unique email, city, and password.

item.name: Log in (admin)
item.description: Set the adminEmail and adminPassword collection variables (Current value) before running. Never save the real password as the Initial value, since that is exported with the collection.

exec: // A unique email, city, and password each run, so the collection can be run repeatedly
pm.test('Logged in as this run\'s user', () => pm.expect(body.user.userId).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('userId'))));
pm.test('Token expires in the future', () => pm.expect(new Date(body.expiresAt).getTime()).to.be.above(Date.now()));
pm.test('At least the 2 new accounts exist', () => pm.expect(page.totalElements).to.be.at.least(2));
pm.test('Shows the updated owner name', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().userName).to.eql('John Smith'));
pm.test('Is not the last page', () => pm.expect(page.last).to.eql(false));

item.name: Search Users by City and State

exec: pm.test('Finds exactly this run\'s user', () => pm.expect(page.content.map(u => u.userId)).to.eql([Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('userId'))]));

item.name: Search Users by Any Single Account
Search Accounts by Balance and Type

exec: pm.test('Every balance is at least 150', () => accounts.forEach(a => pm.expect(a.balance).to.be.at.least(150)));
pm.test('Leads back to the same event', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().referenceId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('auditReference')));
pm.test('Explains the password rule', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().fieldErrors.password).to.include('letter and one number'));

item.name: Unknown email gets the same answer (401)

exec: pm.test('Same message, so emails can\'t be discovered', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('Invalid email or password'));
pm.test('Not theirs', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('You can only access your own accounts'));

item.name: Another customer withdraws from this account (403)
Another customer transfers out of this account (403)
Registering as ADMIN still makes a customer

exec: pm.test('The role in the request is ignored', () => pm.expect(body.user.role).to.eql('CUSTOMER'));
pm.test('Three denied attempts on this account', () => pm.expect(events.length).to.eql(3));
pm.test('Recorded as rejected, with a reason', () => events.forEach(e => { pm.expect(e.outcome).to.eql('REJECTED'); pm.expect(e.reason).to.not.be.empty; }));
pm.test('This run\'s wrong password is on record', () => pm.expect(events.some(e => e.details && e.details.includes(pm.collectionVariables.get('email')))).to.be.true);
pm.test('The deletion succeeded and was recorded', () => pm.expect(events[0].outcome).to.eql('SUCCESS'));
// The earlier event is the refused attempt from 'Delete account with money in it (409)'

pm.test('The earlier refused attempt was recorded too, with a reason', () => { pm.expect(events.length).to.eql(2); pm.expect(events[1].outcome).to.eql('REJECTED'); pm.expect(events[1].reason).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty; });
pm.test('The deletion succeeded and was recorded', () => pm.expect(events[0].outcome).to.eql('SUCCESS'));
// The earlier event is the refused attempt from 'Delete user who still has accounts (409)'
